Yes — the **Chat App** block in `cv.tex` still describes your old **Django Channels** stack (dual Redis, heartbeat presence, channel-layer fan-out). The repo at `/home/duy-hieu/chat` is a different project: a **Go real-time social platform** with a **gateway / dispatcher** split, **SSE for the feed**, and **chat WebSocket + presence planned but not implemented yet**.

Here is how they line up and what I would put on the CV.

## What the CV says vs what you have now

| CV (lines 153–166) | Current project |
|---|---|
| Django Channels, WebSocket | **Go** (`chi`), **SSE** for feed; WebSocket chat is commented as “later milestone” |
| Dual-Redis (channel layer + cache) | **Single Redis** used for **pub/sub** (`internal/pubsub/redis.go`) |
| Heartbeat presence in Redis | **Config only** (`PresenceHeartbeatInterval`, `PresenceTTL`) — no presence package in Go yet |
| Pub/Sub fan-out for status | **Pub/Sub fan-out for post activity** via `feed.Hub` + `subscription.Store` |

What *is* built and worth highlighting:

1. **Two-service architecture** — `cmd/gateway` (long-lived SSE) and `cmd/dispatcher` (auth, future publish path), aligned with your design doc (`cursor_prompt (1).md`).
2. **Refcounted Redis bridge** — `feed.Hub` subscribes to `post:{id}` only while local browsers care, then fans into per-connection channels (`internal/feed/hub.go`).
3. **Gateway-local fan-out** — in-memory store with non-blocking drop policy so one slow client does not block others (`internal/subscription/inmemorystore.go`).
4. **Multiplexed Redis pub/sub** — one connection, many logical subscribers (`internal/pubsub/redis.go`).
5. **Auth foundation** — JWT access + refresh tokens, PostgreSQL via `pgx`, SQL migrations.
6. **Production-minded HTTP** — SSE with keepalives, `WriteTimeout=0`, `access_token` query for `EventSource` (`internal/handlers/sse.go`).

Chat messaging and presence are in the spec and config, but grep shows **no WebSocket or presence implementation in Go yet** — only comments like “Chat WebSocket handlers will live alongside these in a later milestone.”

## How to reframe the project on the CV

Do **not** copy the old Django bullets onto this repo. Either:

- **Option A (honest, strongest today):** Title it as a **real-time social / feed platform** and lead with gateway–dispatcher + SSE + Redis. Mention chat as roadmap only if you have space and label it clearly (“in progress”).
- **Option B:** Keep “Chat App” as the product name but describe the **architecture you are building** (feed + chat domains) and only claim bullets you can defend in an interview.

For backend-focused recruiters, Option A usually reads better because your implemented depth is in **scalable real-time delivery**, not finished Messenger features.

## Suggested replacement block (LaTeX)

You can swap lines 153–166 for something like this (tune wording to your taste):

```latex
\resumeProjectHeading
  {\textbf{Real-Time Social Platform} | \emph{Go, Chi, PostgreSQL, Redis, SSE, Docker, MinIO}}{Solo Project}
\resumeItemListStart
  \resumeItem{\textbf{Goals:} Build a scalable real-time backend with separated gateway and dispatcher services, SSE delivery for feed activity, and a path to WebSocket chat and presence.}
  \resumeItem{\textbf{Deliverables:}}
  \vspace{-2pt}
  \begin{itemize}[leftmargin=0.2in, label=$\vcenter{\hbox{\tiny$\bullet$}}$]
    \small\setlength{\itemsep}{1pt}
    \item Split \textbf{gateway} (SSE connections) and \textbf{dispatcher} (HTTP API, event publish) binaries so long-lived streams and write-path logic scale independently.
    \item Implemented \textbf{home-feed SSE}: refcounted Redis \texttt{SUBSCRIBE} per post via \texttt{feed.Hub}, in-memory per-browser fan-out with drop-on-backpressure, and proxy-safe keepalive comments.
    \item Built a \textbf{Redis pub/sub layer} (multiplexed connection, fan-out to local consumers) behind a \texttt{PubSub} interface for swappable backends.
    \item Added \textbf{JWT auth} (access + refresh tokens) with PostgreSQL persistence, structured logging, and graceful HTTP shutdown.
  \end{itemize}
\resumeItemListEnd
```

If you want one line about the roadmap without overselling:

```latex
\item \textit{In progress:} WebSocket chat, heartbeat-based presence, and dispatcher-to-gateway HTTP routing per system-design.one patterns.
```

Only include that if you are comfortable discussing the design in interviews.

## Technical Skills (line 186–192)

Your skills block still lists **Python/Django** but not **Go**. After updating the project, add Go and Chi (or “Go stdlib + Chi”) and keep PostgreSQL/Redis/Docker. Example tweak:

```latex
\textbf{Languages}{: Go, Python, Java, JavaScript, Node.js} \\
\textbf{Frameworks \& Databases}{: Chi, Django, Express, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis} \\
```

## Interview honesty (mentor note)

The old CV bullets (write-through cache, dual Redis, presence TTL) were strong **if** they matched Django code you could walk through. For this repo, the strongest story is:

- Why gateway and dispatcher are separate.
- How `Hub` avoids tearing down Redis when one of many tabs disconnects.
- Why SSE uses refcount + in-memory store + Redis bridge.
- Trade-off: drop slow clients instead of blocking the bridge.

If you keep “Chat App” as the title but only describe SSE/auth, interviewers may ask “where is chat?” — have a one-sentence answer: “Feed real-time path is implemented; chat WebSocket is the next milestone in the same codebase.”
